nodes.label: tag_strength Formula (6 weighted components)
nodes.rationale: Combines acceptance_rate(0.30), difficulty_score(0.30), rating_boost(0.20), specialization_score(0.10), efficiency_score(0.075), volume_score(0.075) to give a 0-1 strength score per (user,tag), used consistently at both training time (strength.py) and inference time (feature_engineering.py) so scales match.

nodes.label: 82-dim KNN Feature Vector
nodes.rationale: User-level features (rating_boost, efficiency_score) appear once at the end instead of being repeated 20x per tag, to avoid inflating Euclidean distance contributions.

nodes.label: Tag Strength Analysis (peer-benchmarked)
nodes.rationale: TagAnalyzer output (0-100 relative score) is for display only; ML model inputs continue to use absolute tag_strength (0-1) from strength.py to keep training/inference on the same scale.

nodes.label: solve_score Definition
nodes.rationale: solve_score = (ever_ac - wa_count*0.2).clip(-1,1); many wrong answers before solving is treated similarly to not solving at all, so the model predicts 'how cleanly' not just 'will they solve it'.

nodes.label: Sweet Spot Filter (difficulty_match 40-90%)
nodes.rationale: Only recommend problems with solve_score in [-0.2, 0.8] (difficulty_match 40%-90%) to be challenging but reachable, filtering out too-easy and too-hard problems.

nodes.label: Final Ranking Score (weakness_boost + difficulty_match)
nodes.rationale: final_score = 0.6*difficulty_match + 0.4*weakness_boost; problems sorted by weakness_boost first, final_score as tiebreaker, ensuring top results target the user's weakest topics where neighbors are strong.

nodes.label: Attempts Estimation
nodes.rationale: Complements the success model: success model predicts whether a user will solve a problem, attempts model predicts how hard it will be. Shares the same 29-dim feature vector as the success model so both models reuse one inference path.

nodes.label: Attempts Estimator Model (LightGBM)
nodes.rationale: R^2=0.18 is low because 65% of training examples have attempts=1 (solved first try), an extreme right-skew that makes the distribution inherently hard to predict; still useful for relative ranking of problems.

nodes.label: Model Comparison: Rating Progression (LightGBM vs Linear vs Logistic)
nodes.rationale: Logistic Regression performs worse because the heavily skewed continuous target (75% of users have potential <=50pts) loses too much signal when binned into ordinal classes.
nodes.norm_label: model comparison: rating progression (lightgbm vs linear vs logistic)

nodes.label: Model Comparison: Attempts Estimator (LightGBM vs Linear vs Logistic)
nodes.rationale: Logistic Regression achieves negative R^2 (-0.62), worse than predicting the mean; heavily right-skewed target plus binning quantization makes it unsuitable. LightGBM's advantage comes from capturing non-linear interaction between rating_diff and mean_tag_strength.
nodes.norm_label: model comparison: attempts estimator (lightgbm vs linear vs logistic)

nodes.label: KNN Leave-One-Out Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Weakness Recall of 0.86 means 86% of a user's weak tags also appear weak in their KNN neighbors — considered the key driver of recommendation quality.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions Weekly Crawl & Retrain Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs every Sunday 02:00 UTC on GitHub-hosted runners so no dedicated server is required; free tier gives ~2000 min/month and the job takes ~2 hours (~8hrs/month).

nodes.label: ML/preprocessing/submissionsCleaning.py
nodes.rationale: Merges is_tle and is_mle into is_wa, drops unverdicted/null-name rows, drops users with <30 accepted submissions (too sparse for KNN), drops problems with no rating and no tags.

nodes.label: Acceptance Rate Component (Laplace smoothed)
nodes.rationale: acceptance_rate=(ac_count+1)/(total_attempts+2); Laplace smoothing (SMOOTHING=2) prevents division by zero and avoids extreme values for users who tried a tag only once. Weight 0.30 — primary signal for whether the user can actually solve problems in this tag.

nodes.label: Difficulty Score Component
nodes.rationale: difficulty_score=avg_rating_solved/MAX_RATING(3500), clipped to [0,1]. Weight 0.30 — distinguishes someone solving 1000-rated dp from 2500-rated.

nodes.label: Rating Boost Component
nodes.rationale: rating_boost=(cf_rating+cf_max_rating)/(2*MAX_RATING), a user-level constant same across all tags. Weight 0.20 — users with higher ratings are generally stronger everywhere; averages current and max rating to balance current performance with historical best.

nodes.label: Specialization Score Component
nodes.rationale: specialization_score=ac_count/total_ac. Weight 0.10 — depth signal rewarding users who focused on a topic rather than spreading thin.

nodes.label: Efficiency Score Component
nodes.rationale: efficiency_score=first_try_rate, a user-level constant. Weight 0.075 — clean solves indicate genuine mastery.

nodes.label: Volume Score Component
nodes.rationale: volume_score=log(1+ac_count)/log(1+50); uses natural log for diminishing returns (5 vs 0 matters more than 100 vs 110). Weight 0.075 — breadth of practice matters but has diminishing returns.

nodes.label: tag_strength Final Weighted Combination
nodes.rationale: Weights sum to exactly 1.0 across the six components; result clipped to [0,1].

nodes.label: 82-dim Feature Vector Layout (4x20 + 2)
nodes.rationale: tag_strength itself is not used directly in the KNN vector; the 4 component scores are used so distance metric can respond to specific weaknesses (e.g. low acceptance_rate on dp but high difficulty_score).

nodes.label: Internal Similarity Score (rank-based)
nodes.rationale: Maps the K neighbors' distances to [0%,100%] relative to each other; used for weighted tag analysis and problem scoring.

nodes.label: Display Similarity Score (global-max based)
nodes.rationale: Maps against the furthest user in the entire dataset so 100% means identical profile; shown in UI peers table.

nodes.label: TagAnalyzer Acceptance Rate Score (weight 0.35)
nodes.rationale: acc_score = min(user_acceptance_rate/peer_median_acceptance_rate, 1.0); benchmarks user against 50 actual neighbors rather than the whole dataset.

nodes.label: TagAnalyzer Volume Score (weight 0.20)
nodes.rationale: vol_score = 1 - exp(-solved_in_tag/peer_median_solved); exponential ensures diminishing returns, doubling from 5 to 10 matters more than 50 to 100.

nodes.label: weakness_boost Formula
nodes.rationale: weakness_boost = mean((1-user_strength[tag]) * neighbor_strength[tag]) over problem tags; high value means user is weak in a tag AND successful peers are strong in it — the highest-value learning opportunities.

nodes.label: compute_tag_impact()
nodes.rationale: Simulates boosting each of 20 tags by +0.2 (BOOST constant, representing realistic improvement from a few weeks of focused practice), re-runs the success model on 200 candidate problems, counts delta sweet-spot problems, estimates rating gain via delta_problems/10*50 (empirical constant: ~10 extra solvable problems ~= +50 rating points).

nodes.label: Attempts Model Target Variable (wa_count+1)
nodes.rationale: Clipped at 10 to reduce noise from extreme outliers (max in data was 108). Trained on solved problems only since unsolved problems have undefined attempts-to-solve.

nodes.label: Shared 29-dim Feature Vector (Success + Attempts Models)
nodes.rationale: Both models use the identical 29-dim vector so training/inference stay consistent; tag_strength values come from strength.py (not TagAnalyzer.py) to match the [0,1] range used at training time.

nodes.label: Logistic Regression Ordinal-Proxy Technique
nodes.rationale: Since Logistic Regression is a classifier not a regressor, the continuous target is cut into N_BINS=5 equal-frequency bins via np.percentile, multi-class LR is trained on bin labels, and inference recovers a continuous prediction as predict_proba(x) @ bin_midpoints.

nodes.rationale: Spawns .venv/bin/python subprocess running main.py; NumPy types converted to native Python types via a custom convert() function before JSON serialization.

nodes.label: Tag Strength Formula
nodes.rationale: Weighted combination (30% acceptance rate, 30% difficulty score, 20% rating boost, 10% specialization, 7.5% efficiency, 7.5% volume) designed to measure per-topic skill more precisely than raw solve counts; acceptance rate is Laplace-smoothed and volume uses log-diminishing returns to avoid overweighting high-volume grinding.

nodes.label: KNN Peer Matching
nodes.rationale: Uses pure NumPy Euclidean distance over 82-dim vectors (4 stats x 20 tags + 2 scalars) against 2,877 precomputed vectors to find 50 nearest neighbors; chosen for sub-second latency without needing an approximate index, since dataset size is small enough for brute force.

nodes.label: Model 1: Success (solve_score)
nodes.rationale: solve_score = ever_AC - wa_count*0.2, clipped to [-1,1]; the sweet-spot filter keeping predictions in [-0.2, 0.8] is called out as the single most important design decision making recommendations 'challenging but reachable'.

nodes.label: Model 2: Attempts Estimator
nodes.rationale: attempts = wa_count + 1, clipped [1,10], trained on solved-only rows (~307K) and bucketed into easy/moderate/hard for UI labels.

nodes.label: Model 3: Rating Progression (untapped)
nodes.rationale: untapped = cf_max_rating - cf_rating, using 38 features (18 contest-behavior signals + 20 tag strengths) to estimate rating ceiling and support weakness-aware ranking.

nodes.label: Problem Ranking Algorithm
nodes.rationale: final_score = 0.6*difficulty_match + 0.4*weakness_boost; results sorted by weakness_boost first then final_score so skill gaps lead, ensuring recommendations target the user's actual weak tags rather than generic difficulty matching.

nodes.label: Counterfactual Tag Impact Analysis
nodes.rationale: Simulates +20% strength per tag, reruns the success model, counts delta_problems entering the sweet spot, and estimates rating gain to convert model output into a single trustworthy, actionable recommendation (e.g. 'practice dp for +62 rating') rather than a flat list of problems.

nodes.label: Model Comparison vs Linear Baselines
nodes.rationale: LightGBM outperforms Linear Regression and Logistic Regression (used as ordinal-proxy) on both rating progression and attempts tasks; logistic regression collapses with negative R² on skewed continuous targets, demonstrating unsuitability of classification-style baselines for these regression problems.

nodes.label: Web Application Architecture
nodes.rationale: React 19 frontend, Express.js backend proxying CF API and spawning Python subprocess, streams to Gemini; CF data and ML pipeline run in parallel via Promise.allSettled so UI degrades gracefully if the ML pipeline fails.
